doc.overview:
The **Entity Extract** tool analyses a block's source text with a large
language model and records two kinds of stand-off annotation: named entities
(people, organizations, products, locations, and also dates, times,
currencies, and measurements) and terminology candidates (domain-specific
terms that would benefit from a terms entry). Each entity carries a
suggested do-not-translate flag; each term candidate carries a category and a
translatability classification (do-not-translate, consistent, or free). It is
read-only — it writes annotations only and never changes the source or target.

Extraction can optionally combine the LLM with a NER provider for fast entity
detection; the LLM classification is preferred where the two overlap. Blocks
can be analysed one at a time or grouped into batches sent in a single
structured call, and batches can run concurrently. Known terms already in the
terms can be supplied so they are not re-proposed. A provider and, for
hosted providers, credentials are required.

apiKey.help:
Credential for the chosen hosted provider. Required for hosted providers;
not needed for a local Ollama backend.

batchConcurrency.description: Number of batch calls to run in parallel.
batchConcurrency.help:
How many batches are analysed concurrently. A value of 0 or 1 runs batches
sequentially.

batchSize.description: Number of blocks per LLM call.
batchSize.help:
Blocks are grouped into batches of this size and analysed in a single
structured call per batch. A value of 0 or 1 analyses one block per call.

knownTerms.description: Terms to exclude from extraction (already in the terms store).
knownTerms.help:
Terms the LLM is told not to re-propose, so the candidate list focuses on
genuinely new terminology. Matching is case-insensitive.

locale.help:
The locale of the text being analysed, passed to the LLM and any NER
provider so detection is language-aware.

model.help:
The provider-specific model identifier. When omitted, the provider's
default model is used.

limitations: Requires a provider and, for hosted providers, valid credentials; hosted providers make billed, rate-limited network calls.
The NER provider is optional and supplied programmatically; with no NER provider, extraction is LLM-only.
Entity and term suggestions (including the do-not-translate flag and translatability) are model proposals and should be reviewed before acting on them.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks with non-empty source; other parts pass through unchanged.
Read-only — writes entity and term-candidate annotations and never modifies source or target.
When both an LLM and a NER provider produce an entity at the same span, the LLM classification is kept.
Dates, times, currencies, and measurements are not defaulted to do-not-translate, since they need locale-specific formatting.

doc.overview:
The **Term Extract** tool sends each block's source text to a
configured LLM provider and asks it to return notable terms, each with a short
definition and domain. The extracted entries are recorded on the block's
properties as a terminology list. Blocks whose source is empty are skipped, and
blocks with no terms found are left unchanged.

Because the tool calls an external model, it requires provider credentials. An
optional subject domain can be supplied to bias extraction toward that field
(for example medical, legal, or technology terminology). The results are
candidate terms intended for review and curation into a terms store, not
authoritative terminology.

doc.overview:
The **AI Voice Check** tool sends each block's source text to a configured LLM
provider alongside the guidelines a voice profile carries, and reads back
structured findings over four dimensions — tone, style, clarity and brand
compliance — each with a severity, a message and a suggested rewrite. It
computes an overall compliance score, records the score and any findings on the
block's properties, and attaches a `voice` annotation carrying both. A block
whose source text is empty or whitespace-only is skipped.

A voice profile is the context type that says how content should read; a
brand's tone of voice is the common use of it. The profile reaches this tool
three ways: named by `profileId` and resolved from the local store, supplied
already-resolved by the host (the `kapi voice` command, or a project's
`defaults.voice` binding), or resolved lazily from the organizational context
hierarchy on first use. With no profile the prompt carries no guidelines, and
the model is asked to judge against nothing.

This is the judged half of a pair. `voice-vocab-check` is the deterministic
half — the profile's vocabulary and style patterns matched as rules, needing
no credentials and no network — and it is the one to run first, so the model
is spent on what rules cannot decide.

The compliance score and any findings are written to the block's properties, and a `voice` annotation carries both.
A profile that cannot be resolved is not an error, and the run proceeds with no guidelines in the prompt.

doc.overview:
The **AI Voice Inference** tool reads a body of content and proposes the voice
profile it is already written in — the inverse of `voice-check`, which holds
content to a profile that exists. It is the onboarding move: a project that has
been writing in a consistent register for years has a profile, and this reads
it off the corpus rather than asking someone to write it down.

Inference is corpus-level rather than per-block. Every part passes through
unchanged while the tool accumulates each block's source text, and one
inference runs when the input stream ends. The corpus is truncated on a rune
boundary before it is sent, so a large document set costs one bounded request.
An empty stream is not a failure — there is nothing to infer from, and the
tool yields no draft.

The result is a draft in the ordinary voice-profile shape — tone, style,
vocabulary and before/after examples — read from `Draft()` after the flow
completes, together with an evidence sidecar carrying the model's confidence
and a short source note for each top-level field. The evidence stays beside the
profile rather than inside it, so the draft round-trips through the same
`profile.yaml` an author edits by hand. Treat the output as a draft: it is a
proposal to review and commit, not a decided profile.

apiKey.description: API key for the AI provider.
apiKey.help:
Credential for the selected provider. A local provider such as Ollama may
need none. Prefer the credential store or the environment over writing a
key into a recipe.

domain.description: Subject-domain hint woven into the prompt.
domain.help:
A short hint at the subject matter — "medical", "developer tools", "public

maxExamples.description: How many before/after examples the draft may carry.
maxExamples.help:
Caps the rewrite examples requested from the model and kept out of its
response. Defaults to 3.

model.help:
The provider-specific model identifier. Omitted, the provider's default

profileName.help: The name the draft carries. Omitted, the draft is named "Inferred Voice".

provider.help: Selects which model backend performs the inference.

limitations: Requires provider credentials and makes one external API call per run.
The corpus is truncated before it is sent, so a very large content set is inferred from its beginning.
The output is a draft to review; confidence is the model's own estimate, not a measurement.
processingNotes: Every part passes through unchanged; the tool annotates nothing on the content.
The corpus is each block's source text, accumulated over the whole stream; inference runs once, when the stream ends.
An empty or whitespace-only corpus yields no draft rather than an error.

entries.description: Collect blocks into fixed-size batches before forwarding them downstream.

size.title: Batch Size
size.description: Number of blocks to collect before forwarding as a batch

doc.overview:
The **Batch Collector** buffers translatable blocks and forwards them in
groups of a configured size, instead of one at a time. It exists so that a
downstream tool which is cheaper to call in bulk — for example a batch
translation request — can receive several blocks together rather than block
by block.

Non-block parts (layer markers, data, media) pass through immediately and are
never buffered. Blocks accumulate until the batch reaches the configured size
and are then released in order; any remaining blocks are flushed when the
input stream ends. Stream order is preserved.

size.description: Number of blocks to collect before forwarding a batch.
size.help:
The tool buffers blocks until this many have accumulated, then forwards
them as a group. A larger size means fewer, larger handoffs to the next
tool; a size of `1` effectively forwards each block as soon as it arrives.

limitations: Only blocks are batched; all other part types pass through without buffering.
processingNotes: Remaining buffered blocks are flushed when the input stream closes.
Block order within and across batches is preserved.

examples.description: Buffer 50 blocks per handoff for a bulk-friendly downstream tool.

entries.description: Change the letter case of source and/or target text to upper, lower, or title case.

doc.overview:
The **Case Transform** tool rewrites the case of text in translatable blocks.
It can uppercase, lowercase, or title-case the source text, the target text,
or both. It is useful for normalizing display strings — for example forcing
UI labels to upper case — or for preparing case-insensitive comparisons.

When applying to the target, a target locale must be set; the tool only
transforms locales that already have a target. Non-translatable blocks pass
through unchanged.

applySource.description: Apply the transformation to source text.
applySource.help: When enabled, the source text of each translatable block is transformed.

applyTarget.description: Apply the transformation to target text.
applyTarget.help:
When enabled, the target text is transformed for the configured target
locale. A target locale must be set; only existing targets are touched.

mode.help:
Selects the transformation. `upper` converts text to upper case, `lower`
to lower case, and `title` to title case (every letter uppercased, using
the Unicode title-case mapping).

limitations: Title case uses the Unicode title-case mapping applied to every letter, not word-initial capitalization.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks only; non-translatable blocks pass through unchanged.
Target transformation requires a target locale and only affects locales that already have a target.

doc.overview:
The **Create Target** tool ensures every block has a target segment for a
given locale. It is the standard first step when preparing content for
translation: it creates the empty (or source-seeded) target containers that
later tools — translation, leverage, QA — fill and check.

A target locale is required. By default existing targets are left untouched;
enable overwriting to replace them. Targets can be created for
non-translatable blocks as well, which keeps bilingual structure complete
across an entire document.

copySource.description: Seed the new target with the source text.
copySource.help:
When enabled, the source text is copied into the new target segment so it
starts as a duplicate of the source. When disabled, the target is created
empty.

createOnNonTranslatable.description: Also create targets on non-translatable blocks.
createOnNonTranslatable.help:
When enabled, target containers are created even for blocks marked
non-translatable, keeping the bilingual structure complete. Disable it to
skip non-translatable blocks entirely.

overwrite.help:
By default a block that already has a target for the locale is left
unchanged. Enable this to overwrite the existing target with a new
(empty or source-seeded) one.

targetLocale.description: The locale to create a target for.
targetLocale.help:
The BCP-47 locale identifier for the target to create (for example
`fr`). On the CLI and in flows this is typically supplied by the
`--target-lang` value.

processingNotes: Existing targets are skipped unless overwrite is enabled.

entries.description: Reuse translations from a previous document version for unchanged source blocks.

fuzzyMatch.title: Fuzzy Match
fuzzyMatch.description: Enable fuzzy matching for similar texts

doc.overview:
The **Diff Leverage** tool compares each block's source against the same
block in a previous version of the document and carries forward the previous
translation when the source is unchanged. It avoids re-translating content
that has not changed between versions, and tags each block with its diff
status — `new`, `unchanged`, `modified`, or `leveraged`. A target language is
required.

The previous version's source and target texts are supplied programmatically
(keyed by block ID); they are not part of the declarative schema. The two
schema-visible options control how the source comparison is performed.

caseSensitive.help:
When enabled, two sources must match exactly, including letter case, to
count as unchanged. When disabled, the comparison ignores case.

fuzzyMatch.description: Carry forward translations for closely similar sources.
fuzzyMatch.help:
When enabled, a changed source that is sufficiently similar to the
previous version (above an internal similarity threshold) still reuses the
previous translation and is tagged `leveraged` with a similarity score.
When disabled, only exact matches are reused.

limitations: Requires a target language and a previous-version corpus (supplied programmatically); the previous texts are not configurable via the schema.
Fuzzy matching uses a fixed internal similarity threshold.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks only; non-translatable blocks pass through unchanged.
Each block is tagged with a diff-status property; leveraged fuzzy matches also record a similarity score.

examples.description: Carry forward translations where the source is identical.

examples.description: Also reuse translations for closely similar sources.

entries.description: Verify that do-not-translate terms survive verbatim into the target.

caseInsensitive.title: Case-insensitive preservation
caseInsensitive.description: Accept a case-folded match in the target instead of requiring exact case

terms.title: Do-Not-Translate Terms
terms.description: Strings that must survive verbatim into the target (product names

doc.overview:
The **Do-Not-Translate Check** tool guards terms that must reach the target
unchanged — product names, trademarks, code identifiers. For each configured
term that appears in the source as a whole word, it verifies the term is
present verbatim in the target; when it is missing, the block is flagged with a
critical finding (the "the AI translated your product name" case). It is
read-only: it annotates findings and never rewrites content.

The list of protected terms is supplied programmatically rather than as a
schema field — a project, recipe, or checkset provides them, and the terms store
can contribute more. A target locale is required; blocks without a target for
that locale are skipped. The only schema-level option controls whether a
case-folded match in the target is accepted.

caseInsensitive.description: Accept a case-folded match in the target instead of requiring exact case.
caseInsensitive.help:
Off by default, because do-not-translate is usually case-sensitive —
"iPhone" must not become "Iphone". When enabled, a case-insensitive match
in the target satisfies the check.

limitations: The list of protected terms is configured programmatically; it is not exposed as a schema parameter.
A term is only checked when it occurs in the source as a whole word; substrings of larger words are ignored.

When a term is absent from the target the finding records the verbatim term to preserve but proposes no automatic replacement — a miss needs a human or a re-translation, not a blind substring substitution.
Requires a configured target locale; blocks without a target for that locale are skipped.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks that have a target for the configured locale; other parts pass through unchanged.
Findings are emitted in the "do-not-translate" category at critical severity.

examples.title: Case-insensitive preservation
examples.description: Accept a case-folded match for protected terms in the target.

entries.description: Classify the source text of each block as ASCII, UTF-8, or unknown.

doc.overview:
The **Encoding Detect** tool inspects the source text of every translatable
block and records its encoding characteristics on the block's properties: a
detected label (`ascii`, `utf-8`, or `unknown`) plus boolean flags for whether
the text is valid UTF-8 and whether it is ASCII-only. Text that is ASCII-only is
labelled `ascii`; otherwise valid UTF-8 is labelled `utf-8`; anything else is
`unknown`.

The tool takes no configuration. It is useful for spotting non-ASCII content
that may need particular care in downstream formats or fonts, and for
confirming that text is well-formed UTF-8.
limitations: Examines source text only; target translations are not classified.
Detection is limited to ASCII / UTF-8 validity, not a full charset-detection heuristic.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks; non-translatable structure passes through unchanged.

args.title: Arguments
args.description: Command arguments; use ${source} and ${target} as placeholders

sendAsStdin.title: Send as Stdin
sendAsStdin.description: Send text via stdin instead of command arguments

doc.overview:
The **External Command** tool pipes each block's text through an external
command-line program and captures the program's standard output as the new
text. It lets a pipeline reuse an existing CLI filter — a custom normalizer,
a spell-fixer, a transliterator — without writing a native tool.

Text can be sent to the command on standard input or substituted into the
argument list via the `${source}` and `${target}` placeholders. A command is
required, and a target locale is required when applying to the target. Each
invocation has a timeout; the exit code is recorded on the block, and a
non-zero exit leaves the text unchanged and records the error.

**This tool runs code the recipe chooses, so it is gated.** It is exec-class:
a project that names it in a flow runs commands with your privileges and your
environment, and a recipe is bound by entering a directory. kapi therefore
asks once per project, before anything else happens with it, and remembers the
answer; an unattended run with nobody to ask refuses rather than assumes.
`KAPI_TRUST_EXEC=1` grants it where the pipeline author — not the repository
being processed — is the one deciding. The same classification withholds this
tool from the agent surface, from the engine API, and from any recipe arriving
inside a `.kpz`. See
[E-06](/contribute/architecture/engine/e-06-execution-trust).

applySource.help: When enabled, the source text is sent through the command.

applyTarget.help:
When enabled, the target text is sent through the command for the
configured locale. Only existing targets are touched.

dependsOn.condition: required when applyTarget is enabled

args.help:
The argument list for the command. Use `${source}` and `${target}` as
placeholders; both are replaced with the text being processed.

command.help:
Path or name of the command-line program to execute for each block. Its

sendAsStdin.description: Send the text on standard input rather than as an argument.
sendAsStdin.help:

targetLocale.help: The locale whose target text is processed. Required when `applyTarget` is enabled.

dependsOn.condition: must be enabled for this to take effect

timeout.help:
Maximum time to wait for the command to finish for a single block. The
command is cancelled when the timeout elapses.

limitations: A non-zero exit code leaves the text unchanged and records the exit code and error message as block properties.
The command runs once per block per scope (source and/or target), which can be slow for large documents.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks only; non-translatable blocks pass through unchanged.
Trailing newlines are trimmed from the captured output.

doc.overview:
The **Inline Codes Remove** tool removes inline-code runs — placeholders and
paired open/close codes — from segment content, leaving the surrounding plain
text. It is useful when a downstream consumer wants the textual content
without markup, for example to build a plain-text reference or to feed a tool
that cannot handle coded text.

Removal recurses into structured plural and select constructs so inline codes
inside them are also stripped. By default it applies to the target (a target
locale is required) and includes non-translatable blocks. Line-break codes
can optionally be replaced with a space so adjacent words do not run together.

applySource.description: Strip inline codes from source segments.
applySource.help: When enabled, inline-code runs are removed from the source segments.

applyTarget.description: Strip inline codes from target segments.
applyTarget.help:
When enabled, inline-code runs are removed from the target segments of the
configured locale.

dependsOn.condition: required when applyTarget is enabled

includeNonTranslatable.description: Also strip codes from non-translatable blocks.
includeNonTranslatable.help:
When enabled, the removal also applies to blocks marked non-translatable.
Disable it to leave non-translatable blocks untouched.

replaceWithSpace.description: Replace line-break codes with a space instead of removing them.
replaceWithSpace.help:
When enabled, line-break-style placeholder codes are replaced with a single space so that, for example, `foo
bar` becomes `foo bar` rather than `foobar`. Other inline codes are still removed entirely.

targetLocale.help: The locale whose target segments are processed. Required when `applyTarget` is enabled.

dependsOn.condition: must be enabled for this to take effect

limitations: At least one of applySource or applyTarget must be enabled.
processingNotes: Removal recurses into plural and select constructs so codes inside them are stripped as well.
Paired open/close codes are dropped while their inner text content is retained.

entries.description: Apply format-specific tool chains to embedded child layers within a document.

doc.overview:
The **Layer Processor** intercepts embedded child layers — content of one
format nested inside another, such as HTML inside a JSON value — and runs a
format-specific tool chain over the parts of each child layer before emitting
them. It maps a child layer's format name to the chain of tools that should
process that layer's content.

When a child layer's format has no configured chain, its parts pass through
unchanged; non-child-layer parts always pass through. This tool is configured
programmatically: the pipeline-per-format mapping is supplied in Go code, so
it exposes no declarative parameters in flow or CLI configuration.
limitations: Configured programmatically only; the format-to-pipeline mapping is not expressible via flow or CLI config.
Only embedded child layers are intercepted; top-level layers and their parts pass through.
processingNotes: Parts of a child layer are buffered until the layer ends, then processed through the matching tool chain and re-emitted in order.
Child layers whose format has no configured pipeline pass through unchanged.

The **Placeholder Check** tool verifies that every interpolation placeholder
in the source survives, by count, into the target. A dropped `{count}` or an
unbalanced `<0>` is the kind of break that crashes a translated application at
runtime, so a placeholder present fewer times in the target than in the source
is flagged as critical. It is read-only: it annotates findings and never
rewrites content.

Placeholders are detected with a built-in pattern covering the common
interpolation styles — `{{name}}`, `${name}`, `%(name)s` (Python),
`%1$s` (positional), `%s` / `%d` / `%@` (printf / Objective-C),
`{name}` / `{0}` (ICU / .NET), and numbered tags such as `<0>…</0>`. A target
locale is required; blocks without a target for that locale are skipped.

flagExtra.description: Report placeholders present in the target but absent from the source.
flagExtra.help:
When enabled (the default), a placeholder that appears in the target but
not the source — usually a stray token — is reported as a major issue, in
addition to the always-critical report of placeholders dropped from the
target.

limitations: Detection is pattern-based and covers the common interpolation styles listed above; placeholder syntaxes outside that set are not recognised.
The check compares placeholder counts, not positions; a placeholder present the correct number of times but in the wrong order is not flagged.
Requires a configured target locale; blocks without a target for that locale are skipped.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks that have a target for the configured locale; other parts pass through unchanged.
Dropped placeholders are reported at critical severity; extra placeholders (when flagExtra is enabled) at major severity.

doc.overview:
The **Pseudo Translate** tool produces fake translations that exercise a
product's handling of translated text without a real translator. It replaces
ASCII letters with accented look-alikes, wraps each segment in marker
characters, and can pad the text to simulate the length growth of a real
translation. The result reveals hard-coded strings, clipped layouts, and
encoding problems before translation begins. A target language is required
(the conventional pseudo locale is `qps`).

Inline codes and placeholders are protected: text inside `{...}` markers and
non-text runs are passed through unchanged so the runtime can still substitute
parameters. The transform is deterministic, so the same input always yields
the same output.

expansionPercent.description: Extra padding to simulate translation expansion.
expansionPercent.help:
Adds padding characters proportional to the text length, so the output is
longer than the source — a common effect of real translation. A value of
0 adds no padding.

prefix.description: Characters prepended to each translated segment.
prefix.help:
A marker placed before the pseudo-translated text. The default shade
marker makes the segment boundary visible so untranslated, concatenated,
or clipped strings stand out.

suffix.description: Characters appended to each translated segment.
suffix.help: A marker placed after the pseudo-translated text, mirroring the prefix.

limitations: Only ASCII letters are accented; other characters and content inside `{...}` placeholder markers are passed through unchanged.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks with a non-empty source; other parts pass through unchanged.
Inline codes and placeholders are preserved; the prefix/suffix wrap the whole segment once.
With a session cache, already-pseudo-translated targets are reused and fresh results are written back.

doc.overview:
The **Quality Check** tool runs a battery of rule-based checks over each
translation and records the findings on the block's properties as a JSON array
of QA issues, along with a pass/fail flag. The checks span several categories:
general text issues (empty target, whitespace mismatches, double spaces,
doubled words, target identical to source, corrupted characters), inline-code
consistency, span constraint violations, regex pattern preservation, and length
ratios. A target locale is required; when a block has no translation, only the
empty-target check applies.

With no `--provider`, the checks are deterministic and need no credentials.
Setting `--provider` instead runs LLM-judged QA: the chosen model reviews each
translation for terminology, fluency, and accuracy. The rule-based toggles
below apply to the deterministic mode; `model` and `checks` apply to the LLM
mode. Every rule check can be toggled independently, and the length checks
share the long/short ratio model used by the dedicated length-check tool.

absoluteMaxCharLength.description: Maximum number of characters allowed in any target segment.
absoluteMaxCharLength.help: The absolute character cap used by the absolute-maximum-length check.

dependsOn.condition: must be enabled for this limit to take effect

apiKey.description: API key for the LLM provider (LLM mode).
apiKey.help: Credential for the chosen hosted provider when `--provider` selects one.

checkAbsoluteMaxCharLength.description: Flag target segments that exceed an absolute character count limit.
checkAbsoluteMaxCharLength.help:
When enabled, the target is flagged when it exceeds the absolute character
count given by `absoluteMaxCharLength`, independent of source length.

dependsOn.condition: sets the limit applied when this check is enabled

checkCodeDifference.description: Verify that the target has the same inline codes as the source.
checkCodeDifference.help:
Flags warnings when inline codes are missing from or extra in the target
compared with the source, counted by code type.

checkCorruptedCharacters.description: Check for patterns indicating encoding corruption.
checkCorruptedCharacters.help:
Flags a warning when the target contains characters that suggest encoding
corruption (for example UTF-8 misread as ISO-8859-1, signalled by the
Unicode replacement character).

checkDoubleSpaces.description: Check for double spaces in the target.
checkDoubleSpaces.help: Flags a warning when the target contains two consecutive spaces.

checkDoubledWord.description: Check for consecutive repeated words in the target.
checkDoubledWord.help:
Flags a warning when the same word appears twice in a row in the target,
unless the word is listed in `doubledWordExceptions`.

checkEmptySource.description: Warn when the target is non-empty but the source is empty.
checkEmptySource.help: Flags a warning when the target has content but the source is empty.

checkEmptyTarget.description: Warn when the target is empty but the source has content.
checkEmptyTarget.help:
Flags an error when a block has source content but no (or empty) target
text. This is the one check that still applies when a block has no
translation at all.

checkLeadingWhitespace.description: Check for leading-whitespace mismatches between source and target.
checkLeadingWhitespace.help:
Flags a warning when the leading whitespace of the target differs from that
of the source.

checkMaxCharLength.description: Flag targets longer than a percentage of source character length.
checkMaxCharLength.help:
Enables the maximum length-ratio check, using a long/short model: the
allowed percentage depends on whether the source is above or below the
maximum breakpoint.

checkMinCharLength.description: Flag targets shorter than a percentage of source character length.
checkMinCharLength.help:
Enables the minimum length-ratio check, using a long/short model: the
required percentage depends on whether the source is above or below the
minimum breakpoint.

checkPatterns.description: Verify that source patterns have expected corresponding content in the target.
checkPatterns.help:
When enabled, configured source/target regex pattern pairs are checked so
that patterns found in the source are preserved in the target. The pattern
pairs themselves are supplied programmatically.

checkSpanConstraints.description: Check non-deletable and non-cloneable span constraint violations.
checkSpanConstraints.help:
Flags an error when a non-deletable inline code is missing from the target,
or a non-cloneable inline code is duplicated in the target, according to the
per-code constraints carried on the source runs.

checkTargetSameAsSource.description: Warn when the target is identical to the source.
checkTargetSameAsSource.help:
Flags a warning when the target text equals the source text and contains at
least one letter or digit. Number-only segments are governed by
`targetSameAsSourceWithNumbers`.

checkTerminology.help: Enables terminology verification within QA check. Disabled by default.

checkTrailingWhitespace.description: Check for trailing-whitespace mismatches between source and target.
checkTrailingWhitespace.help:
Flags a warning when the trailing whitespace of the target differs from that
of the source.

checks.description: Quality dimensions for the LLM judge (LLM mode).
checks.help:
The list of quality dimensions the LLM evaluates, e.g. terminology,
fluency, accuracy, consistency. Defaults to terminology, fluency, accuracy.

doubledWordExceptions.help:
A semicolon-separated list of words that may legitimately appear twice in a
row (for example certain pronouns), so they are not flagged by the
doubled-word check.

dependsOn.condition: only consulted when the doubled-word check is enabled

maxCharLengthAbove.description: Maximum allowed percentage of source length for long text.
maxCharLengthAbove.help: The maximum target/source ratio applied when the source is long.

maxCharLengthBelow.description: Maximum allowed percentage of source length for short text.
maxCharLengthBelow.help: The maximum target/source ratio applied when the source is short.

maxCharLengthBreak.description: Character count above which text is considered long (max check).
maxCharLengthBreak.help:
Source text longer than this is treated as long for the maximum-ratio check;
shorter text is treated as short.

minCharLengthAbove.description: Minimum required percentage of source length for long text.
minCharLengthAbove.help: The minimum target/source ratio applied when the source is long.

minCharLengthBelow.description: Minimum required percentage of source length for short text.
minCharLengthBelow.help: The minimum target/source ratio applied when the source is short.

minCharLengthBreak.description: Character count above which text is considered long (min check).
minCharLengthBreak.help:
Source text longer than this is treated as long for the minimum-ratio check;
shorter text is treated as short.

model.description: The model name to request (LLM mode).
model.help:
The provider-specific model identifier for LLM-judged QA. When omitted, the
provider's default model is used.

provider.description: LLM provider for AI-judged QA (omit for rule-based checks).
provider.help:
When set, QA runs as an LLM judge using this provider instead of the
deterministic rule checks. Options are populated from the provider
registry. Leave empty to run the rule-based checks with no credentials.

strictCodeOrder.description: Flag differences when codes appear in a different order.
strictCodeOrder.help:
When enabled, and no count differences were found, the target is flagged if
its inline codes appear in a different order than in the source.

dependsOn.condition: the order check runs alongside code-difference checking

targetSameAsSourceWithCodes.description: Include inline codes when comparing source and target for identity.
targetSameAsSourceWithCodes.help:
Controls whether inline codes are taken into account in the
same-as-source comparison.

targetSameAsSourceWithNumbers.description: Include number-only segments in the same-as-source comparison.
targetSameAsSourceWithNumbers.help:
When enabled, segments containing only numbers (and punctuation) are
included in the target-same-as-source check. Disable it to ignore
number-only segments, which are often legitimately identical.

limitations: Length and ratio checks compare character lengths only when source and target are both non-empty.
The regex pattern pairs used by `checkPatterns` are supplied programmatically, not as schema parameters.
Requires a configured target locale.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks; non-translatable structure passes through unchanged.
When a block has no translation, only the empty-target check applies.
Findings are stored on the block as a JSON array of QA issues with a pass/fail flag.

doc.overview:
The **Recycle** tool queries a content memory (Memory) for each block's
source text and pre-fills the target with the best match. It tries an exact
match first, then a fuzzy match above a configurable threshold, recording the
match score and type (`exact` or `fuzzy`) on the block. It requires a target
language and a content-memory provider; without a content memory the tool has nothing to leverage.

Whether a match is written into the target is governed by a fill threshold
and an "only if empty" option, so high-confidence matches can be applied while
weaker ones are recorded but left for review. A no-query threshold lets the
tool skip the content-memory lookup when an existing candidate already scores high enough.
Optionally, all leveraged matches can be written to a TMX file.

downgradeIdenticalBestMatches.description: Reduce the score when multiple identical exact matches exist.
downgradeIdenticalBestMatches.help:
When enabled, an exact match is scored 99 instead of 100 if the content memory returns
multiple identical best matches, flagging the ambiguity for review.

fillIfTargetIsEmpty.description: Only fill the target when it has no existing content.
fillIfTargetIsEmpty.help:
When enabled, a match is written only if the block's target is currently
empty, so existing translations are never overwritten.

fillTarget.description: Copy the best match into the target.
fillTarget.help:
When enabled, the best qualifying match is written into the block's
target content. When disabled, matches are scored and recorded but the
target is not filled.

fillTargetThreshold.description: Minimum match score required to fill the target.
fillTargetThreshold.help:
A match must score at least this value to be written into the target.
Matches between the fuzzy threshold and this value are recorded but not
filled.

dependsOn.condition: filling must be enabled for this threshold to apply

fuzzyThreshold.description: Minimum score for a fuzzy match to be considered.
fuzzyThreshold.help:
The lowest fuzzy-match score (0-100) the content-memory lookup will return. Matches
below this score are ignored.

makeTmx.description: Generate a TMX document of leveraged matches.
makeTmx.help:
When enabled, all leveraged matches are written to a TMX file at the
configured output path.

dependsOn.condition: set the output path when generating TMX

noQueryThreshold.description: Skip the content memory query when an existing candidate scores high enough.
noQueryThreshold.help:
If the block already carries a match score at or above this value, the content memory
lookup is skipped. The default of 101 means the content memory is always queried.

tmxPath.description: Output path for the generated TMX document.
tmxPath.help: File path where the TMX document is written when TMX generation is enabled.

dependsOn.condition: TMX generation must be enabled

limitations: Requires a target language and a content-memory provider; with no Memory there is nothing to leverage.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks with a non-empty source; other parts pass through unchanged.
Exact matches are tried before fuzzy matches; the match score and type are recorded as block properties.

With a structure-aware content-memory provider, matching runs against the block's inline-code structure and fills carry the matched entry's runs, so markup placeholders survive the fill; a 100% match means text and structure agree.
Ambiguous matches (several full-score entries with differing targets) are recorded but never fill the target — the choice surfaces for review instead of being picked by storage order.

doc.overview:
The **Redact** tool replaces sensitive spans in the source with protected
placeholders before the content is processed (for example, before it is sent
to a translation provider), and stashes the originals locally so a later
`unredact` can restore them. It never emits the original value into the
rewritten content. It is a recoverable transformer: it produces an edit plan
— the span replacements plus the originals to vault — and the framework
applier rewrites the source, rebasing surviving run-anchored overlays so an
upstream annotator's terms or entities follow the rewrite.

Two detection backends can run, alone or together: `rules` matches literal
terms and regular expressions from a rules file or inline rules, and
`entities` redacts entity annotations already on the block (as produced by
`entity-extract`). When no detector is configured, `rules` is used. The
originals are stored on the block as an in-process secret annotation by
default, or written to a sidecar vault when a vault path is supplied (the
external mode used by `extract` → `merge`).

detectors.description: Detection backends to run: rules and/or entities.
detectors.help:
`rules` matches literal terms and regular expressions from a rules file or
inline rules. `entities` redacts entity annotations already attached to the
block (e.g. by `entity-extract`). Both may be listed; when none is set,
`rules` is used.

entityTypes.description: Entity categories to redact when the `entities` detector is enabled.
entityTypes.help:
Restricts entity redaction to the listed categories. When unset, the
default set is person, organization, product, and location — dates, times,
currencies, and measurements are intentionally excluded because they need
locale-specific formatting rather than hiding.
entityTypes.values: list of entity categories (default `[person, organization, product, location]`)

dependsOn.condition: the `entities` detector must be enabled

placeholder.description: Visible stand-in template for redacted spans.
placeholder.help:
The template used to render the visible placeholder that replaces each
redacted span. It supports `{category}` (the detected category) and `{n}`
(a per-category counter). When unset, the framework default template is
used.

rulesPath.description: Path to a redaction rules YAML file.
rulesPath.help:
Loads literal terms and regular expressions to redact. Only relevant when
the `rules` detector is enabled. A rules file may also define its own
placeholder template, which is used unless the tool's `placeholder` is set.

dependsOn.condition: the `rules` detector must be enabled

limitations: The `entities` detector only acts on entity annotations already present on the block; it does not detect entities itself — pair it with `entity-extract`.
Inline rules and the sidecar vault path are supplied programmatically by callers (e.g. extract → merge) rather than through the schema fields documented here.
Operates on translatable source spans; dates, times, currencies, and measurements are excluded from the default entity set.
processingNotes: A recoverable transformer — it returns an edit plan and the framework applier rewrites the source, rebasing surviving overlays across the rewrite. The placement pass requires it to run before any step that sends source to a remote sink.
Originals are recorded as an in-process secret annotation by default, or in a sidecar vault when a vault path is supplied (external mode); the applier vaults them atomically with the rewrite.
A later `unredact` reads the recovery record to restore the originals.

The **Remove Target** tool deletes target segments from blocks. With a target
locale set, it removes only that locale's targets; with no locale, it removes
all targets. It is useful for resetting translations before a fresh run, or
for clearing targets in a specific locale.

Removal can be scoped to specific text units by ID, which restricts the
operation to a comma-separated list of block IDs. Optionally, a block whose
targets are all removed can itself be dropped from the stream.

filterByIDs.description: Filter text units by ID rather than by locale alone.

When enabled, removal is restricted to the blocks listed in
`textUnitIDs`. When disabled, removal is driven by the target locale
across all blocks.

removeBlockIfEmpty.description: Drop a block when it has no targets left.
removeBlockIfEmpty.help:
When enabled, a block that has no remaining target segments after removal
is dropped from the stream entirely. When disabled, the now-empty block is
kept.

targetLocale.help:
The locale to clear. When empty, the targets for every locale on the
block are removed.

textUnitIDs.help:
A comma-delimited list of block (text-unit) IDs. When set and ID
filtering is enabled, only blocks whose ID appears in the list have their
targets removed. Leave empty to remove targets from all blocks.

doc.overview:
The **Review** tool asks a configured LLM provider to review each
translation and return a concise assessment: a score from 1 to 10, a brief
judgement of accuracy and fluency, and a suggested improvement where warranted.
The review text is recorded on the block's properties along with the provider
name. Blocks without a translation for the target locale are skipped.

Both a target locale and provider credentials are required, since the tool makes
an external API call per block. Unlike the AI QA check, which returns structured
issues, this tool produces a free-form review intended for human reviewers
deciding whether a translation needs revision.

The review is free-form model output, not structured QA issues.
Blocks without a translation for the target locale are skipped.
processingNotes: Operates on blocks that have a translation for the target locale.
Blocks are processed in parallel by default for throughput.
The review text and provider name are stored on the block's properties.

doc.overview:
The **Script** tool runs a user-provided ES5 JavaScript program for every
part in the stream. The script receives the current part as a `part` object
and can read and modify block source and target text. It is an escape hatch
for bespoke transformations that no built-in tool covers.

Inside the script, `part.type` identifies the part and `part.block` exposes
the block (with `id`, `translatable`, `source`, and `targets`). Helper
functions are available: `emit(part)` forwards a part, `skip()` drops the
current part, and `log(msg)` writes a message to standard error. When the
script neither emits nor skips, the part passes through with any in-place
text edits applied. The script is provided inline or read from a `.js` file.

**This tool runs code the recipe chooses, so it is gated.** It is exec-class:
the script is recipe-supplied, `file` reads a path the recipe names, and a
recipe is bound by entering a directory. kapi therefore asks once per project,
before anything else happens with it, and remembers the answer; an unattended
run with nobody to ask refuses rather than assumes. `KAPI_TRUST_EXEC=1` grants
it where the pipeline author — not the repository being processed — is the one
deciding. The same classification withholds this tool from the agent surface,
from the engine API, and from any recipe arriving inside a `.kpz`. See
[E-06](/contribute/architecture/engine/e-06-execution-trust).

A part passes through unchanged when the script neither emits a part nor calls skip.

doc.overview:
The **Segmentation** tool splits a block's text into sentence-level segments.
Segmentation determines the unit of translation and of content-memory
matching, so consistent segmentation is important for leverage and review.
By default the tool segments source text using built-in SRX-style rules that
handle common sentence boundaries and abbreviations; rules can also be loaded
from an SRX file.

The number of segments produced is recorded on each block. Already-segmented
text is left alone unless re-segmentation is requested. Target text can be
segmented independently, with its own rules file.

overwriteSegmentation.help:
By default text that already has more than one segment is left untouched.
Enable this to discard the existing segmentation and re-segment.

renumberCodes.description: Renumber inline-code IDs within each segment.
renumberCodes.help:
When enabled, inline-code IDs are renumbered to start at 1 within each
resulting segment.

segmentSource.help:
When enabled, the source text is split into segments using the source
rules. If neither source nor target segmentation is enabled, source
segmentation is applied by default.

segmentTarget.help:
When enabled, existing target text for the configured locale is split
into segments using the target rules.

sourceSrxPath.description: Path to an SRX rules file for the source.
sourceSrxPath.help:
Path to an SRX segmentation rules file used for the source text. When
empty, the built-in default rules are used.

targetSrxPath.description: Path to an SRX rules file for the target.
targetSrxPath.help:
Path to an SRX segmentation rules file used for the target text. When
empty, the built-in default rules are used.

treatIsolatedCodesAsWhitespace.description: Treat isolated inline codes as whitespace while segmenting.
treatIsolatedCodesAsWhitespace.help:
When enabled, an isolated inline code is treated like whitespace for the
purpose of finding segment boundaries.

processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks only; non-translatable blocks pass through unchanged.
The resulting segment count is written to a block property.

entries.description: Reclassify generic markup inline codes into semantic vocabulary types.

doc.overview:
The **Span Classify** tool reclassifies generic `code:markup` inline codes —
placeholders and paired open/close codes — into proper semantic vocabulary
types such as bold, italic, hyperlink, or image. It is designed to run after
readers that emit generic markup codes (for example bridge XLIFF or Okapi
readers), so that later tools and editors see meaningful inline-code types
rather than opaque markup.

Classification uses two strategies: a map of known Okapi code sub-types, and,
failing that, the HTML element name parsed from the code's raw data. When a
semantic type is resolved, the tool also applies the vocabulary's display
form, equivalence text, and editing constraints. Codes it cannot classify are
left as they are. The tool has no configurable parameters.
limitations: Classification covers known Okapi sub-types and common HTML elements; unrecognized codes are left unchanged.
Has no configurable parameters.
processingNotes: Operates on inline-code runs in both source and target segments.
Recurses into plural and select constructs so codes inside them are classified as well.

doc.overview:
The **Tag Protect** tool finds tags and placeholders in source text using
regular-expression patterns and records them as an annotation on the block,
along with a count property. Downstream tools — for example an MT or AI
translation step — can then read the annotation to preserve those tokens
rather than translating or reformatting them.

When no patterns are configured, a built-in default set is used, covering
HTML/XML tags, curly-brace placeholders (ICU, Java, .NET), printf-style
placeholders, and `${...}` template expressions. The tool records what it
found; preserving the matches is the job of the consuming tool.

patterns.description: Regular-expression patterns for tags and placeholders to protect.
patterns.help:
A list of regular expressions; any substring of the source matching a
pattern is recorded as a protected tag. When the list is empty, a
built-in default set is used (HTML/XML tags, curly-brace placeholders,
printf-style placeholders, and `${...}` template expressions).
patterns.values: array of regular expressions (default: built-in set)

limitations: Patterns use Go's RE2 syntax, which does not support backreferences or lookaround.
The tool records protected matches as an annotation; it does not itself prevent their modification.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks only; non-translatable blocks pass through unchanged.
Matches are recorded as a block annotation and the match count as a block property; matches are deduplicated and ordered by offset.

entries.description: Verify that required target terms appear when their source terms are present.

doc.overview:
The **Terminology Check** tool checks each translation against a set of
source/target term pairs. For every entry, if the source term occurs in the
block's source text, the tool verifies that the required target term occurs in
the translation; when it does not, the block is flagged and the missing
expectations are recorded on its properties. A target locale is required, and a
terms store supplies the term pairs.

The term pairs are supplied programmatically rather than as a schema field, so
the tool is typically wired up by the host application or a project that binds
a terms store. The only schema-level option controls whether term matching
respects letter case.

caseSensitive.help:
When enabled, source and target terms must match exactly, including letter
case. When disabled, matching is case-insensitive, so a term matches
regardless of how it is capitalised in the text.

limitations: The set of term pairs is configured programmatically; it is not exposed as a schema parameter.
Matching is substring-based; it does not account for inflection or morphology.
Requires a configured target locale and a terms store; blocks without a translation are skipped.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks; non-translatable structure passes through unchanged.
Only entries whose source term is present in the block's source are checked.

doc.overview:
The **Translate** tool translates untranslated block content. A single
`--provider` selects the backend: a large-language-model provider (Anthropic,
OpenAI, Gemini, Azure OpenAI, Ollama) or the keyless offline demo provider.
Classic machine-translation engines are not built in; a plugin can register
one, and it is then selected the same way. The result is written as the target
text, with an alternate-translation annotation recording the originating
provider. A target language is required, and credentials are required for
hosted providers (local Ollama and the offline demo need none).

Blocks that contain inline codes are sent through a placeholder-preserving
prompt so tags survive translation, then reconstructed from the response.
Blocks can be translated one at a time or grouped into batches sent in a
single structured call; batches can run concurrently. When run with a session
cache, already-translated targets are reused and fresh translations are
written back, so repeat runs skip work already done.

and the demo provider run locally. The available options are populated

toolMeta.description: Restore original values into redacted content after processing

doc.overview:
The **Unredact** tool reverses `redact`: it restores the original values into
the redaction placeholders across a block's source and target runs, then
removes the in-process secret annotation so nothing sensitive reaches the
writer. It is the closing half of the redact → process → unredact cycle, run
after the protected content has been processed (for example, translated).

Restoration uses the recovery record left by `redact`. By default it reads the
in-process secret annotation on the block; in external mode it reads originals
from a sidecar vault (used by the `extract` → `merge` workflow). Both an
ID-based restore (for structure-preserving formats and inline codes) and a
text-based restore (for formats that flattened a placeholder to its visible
string on write) are applied, so placeholders are recovered in either case.
The vault path is supplied programmatically by the caller rather than as a
schema field, so this tool exposes no schema parameters.
limitations: Exposes no schema parameters; the optional sidecar vault path is supplied programmatically by callers (e.g. extract → merge).
Restores only placeholders recorded by a preceding `redact` run; there is nothing to restore without that recovery record.
processingNotes: A transformer that restores originals into both source and target runs — it returns an edit plan and the framework applier rewrites the block, rebasing surviving source overlays across the restore.
Reads the in-process secret annotation by default, or a sidecar vault in external mode.
Removes the secret annotation after restoring, so sensitive originals never reach the writer.

entries.description: Flag forbidden, competitor and retired wording from a voice profile and the project's terms.

doc.overview:
The **Voice Vocabulary Check** tool is the deterministic gate a voice profile
carries: the forbidden terms, the competitor terms and the prohibited style
patterns, matched over each block's source text with no model and no network.
A forbidden term reports at major severity and a competitor term at critical,
each defaulting from the profile and overridable per rule; where the rule names
a replacement, the finding carries it as the suggestion. Terms match whole-word
and Unicode-aware, so `use` never fires inside `user`; style patterns match as
the regular expression the author wrote them as.

When the project binds a terms store, the tool enforces that too — the
vocabulary the project *decided*, alongside the lists the profile carries. A
competitor entry reports critical, a forbidden one major and a retired one
minor, the softer reading for a word that was the project's own until a
decision replaced it. The alternative comes from the concept: its preferred
term in the same language, or the replacement the term's note names. Lookup
asks in the block's own language and, when that names a region, in the bare
language beneath it, so a project writing `en-GB` is still held to a decision
recorded as `en`.

Findings and an overall score are attached as a `voice` annotation. The profile
and the terms store are supplied by the host rather than by step configuration:
a recipe names this tool as a step (`kapi init` scaffolds exactly that) and the
project's `defaults.voice` binding decides what it enforces. The standalone
command is `kapi check --profile`.

This is the half to run before `voice-check`, its LLM-judged sibling: what a
rule can decide should not be spent on a model.
limitations: The profile and the terms store are supplied programmatically; neither is a schema parameter.
Matching is lexical — whole-word and case-insensitive, with no account of inflection or morphology.
Judges source text only, and skips a block whose source is empty or whitespace-only.
Required style patterns are a document-scope question and are evaluated by the check venue, not here.
processingNotes: Operates on blocks; a block with no findings is left unannotated.
Monolingual by declaration, because it reads the source — a bilingual declaration would yield no pass at all on a project with no target languages.
A term recorded in both a regional and a bare language is one decision and reports once.
Every finding carries the run range it matched, so a preview can highlight the exact words.

doc.overview:
The **Whitespace Correct** tool cleans up whitespace in target translations.
It can collapse repeated spaces, trim leading and trailing whitespace, match
the source's leading/trailing whitespace onto the target, remove zero-width
characters, and remove whitespace after specific punctuation marks. The last
is particularly useful when translating from a space-delimited language into a
non-space-delimited one such as Chinese or Japanese.

The tool operates only on the target text, so a target locale is required, and
only blocks that already have a target for that locale are processed.

is removed, per the included whitespace types.

correctExclamation.help:

full-width `！`) is removed, per the included whitespace types.

correctFullStop.help:
When enabled, whitespace following a full stop (ASCII `.` or full-width
`．`) is removed, per the included whitespace types.

correctQuestion.help:
When enabled, whitespace following a question mark (ASCII `?` or
full-width `？`) is removed, per the included whitespace types.

includeHorizontalWS.help:
When enabled, horizontal tab characters are treated as removable after
punctuation.

includeVerticalWS.help:
When enabled, vertical whitespace — line feeds and carriage returns — is
treated as removable after punctuation.

source's edge whitespace.

doc.overview:
The **XML Validation** tool checks the source and, optionally, target text of
each translatable block for XML well-formedness and records the result on the
block's properties: a validity flag and, when invalid, an error message
identifying whether the source or target failed and why. Empty text is treated
as valid.

Source validation is on by default. To validate the target as well, enable the
target check and supply a target locale. Because block text is often an XML
fragment rather than a complete document, the tool can wrap the text in a root
element before parsing so a fragment with multiple top-level nodes still
validates.

checkSource.description: Validate source text for XML well-formedness.
checkSource.help:
When enabled, each block's source text is parsed as XML and any
well-formedness error is reported.

checkTarget.description: Validate target text for XML well-formedness.
checkTarget.help:
When enabled, the target translation is parsed as XML in addition to the
source. A target locale must be supplied when this is enabled.

dependsOn.condition: only used when target checking is enabled

wrapRoot.description: Wrap text in a root element before validating.
wrapRoot.help:
When enabled, the text is wrapped in a synthetic root element before
parsing, so a fragment with several top-level nodes (which is not a valid
standalone document) still validates. Disable it to require a single
well-formed document.

limitations: Checks well-formedness only; it does not validate against a DTD or schema.
Empty source or target text is treated as valid.
processingNotes: Operates on translatable blocks; non-translatable structure passes through unchanged.

examples.title: Validate source only
examples.description: Confirm the source text of each block parses as XML.

examples.title: Validate target as well
examples.description: Also validate the French translation, treating each block as a fragment.
